content.text:
What I checked
- You were running as root (whoami => root).
- The sudo group existed but /etc/sudoers had no %sudo entry, so members of the sudo group were not granted sudo rights.

What I changed
- I added the standard sudoers line for the sudo group:
  %sudo ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL
- I validated the file with visudo; it parsed OK.

What to do next (if you want a non-root user to be able to use sudo)
- Add the user to the sudo group (replace username):
  usermod -aG sudo username
- Have the user log out and log back in (or reboot) so the new group membership takes effect.
- Verify the user can use sudo:
  sudo -l   (run as that user)

If you prefer, I can instead add a specific user directly to sudoers via visudo.

{"answer":"Cause: /etc/sudoers had no entry granting the sudo group sudo rights, so users in group sudo couldn’t run sudo.
What I did: added the standard line to /etc/sudoers and validated it with visudo:
  %sudo ALL=(ALL:ALL) ALL
What you should do next to allow a specific user to use sudo:
  1) Add the user to the sudo group: usermod -aG sudo <username>
  2) Have the user log out and log back in (or reboot) so group membership is re-evaluated.
  3) Verify as that user: sudo -l
Alternative: add a single user to sudoers with visudo if you prefer not to use the sudo group.
